messages:
mike_sales: Heads-up: NordicLedger (prospect) submitted a security addendum for the POC. Key asks: strict EU-only processing for POC, BYOK for KMS, full list of EU subprocessors, and a fixed-region dedicated option during the trial. they want to kick off in ~3 business days.

solutions_rina: can you paste the exact excerpt so we can align language? also do they want an irrevocable contractual guarantee or an operational attestation for the short POC?

mike_sales: excerpt: "All data processed during the POC must not leave EU territories. Customer requires BYOK for encryption keys and a vendor subprocessor list with EU residency statements." they indicated "contractual assurance" but open to an attestation for POC.

ops_julie: short: we can pin serving to eu-west-1 / eu-west-3 for POC and ensure KV/cache stays in-region. caveat: our hosted control plane currently runs multi-region; some non-customer metadata (billing & deploy orchestration) may route to control plane endpoints in us-*. can document and limit what is sent.

sec_omar: important: define scope of "data" — e.g., request/response payloads vs control-plane telemetry. we need to call out telemetry, logs, and crash dumps. for POC we can suppress debug-level telemetry and provide retention <= 7 days as a condition.

infra_tom: routing policy example we can use for the POC: 
```
route_policy: "region_pin"
region: "eu-west-1"
fallback: "eu-fallback"
```
This pins model serving, model cache and KV to the specified eu region. note: if they require zero cross-border egress we should avoid hosted control plane changes during the POC or run Private.

prod_elena: pricing/ops note: spinning a temporary dedicated pool for 2 weeks has an infra delta. estimate +15% hourly vs shared hosted for short leases (covers warm GPUs). full BYOK onboarding adds ~1 engineer-day + config checks.

mike_sales: timeline problem: BYOK onboarding estimate 3-5 business days — they want start in 3bd. any quicker option?

sec_omar: possible fast path: ephemeral customer-isolated keys generated by our onboarding flow (we hold key material but create per-tenant envelopes) — faster, no full HSM BYOK. security can greenlight if customer signs a POC scoping waiver restricting data types.

legal_sam: for contractual language: we can offer a POC attestation (signed subprocessors snapshot + limited scoping addendum). if they want contractual zero-egress guarantee we need Private deployment + specific indemnities; that won't fly for hosted POC.

solutions_rina: i'll draft the one-page POC checklist for NordicLedger. includes: region_pin config, key approach options (ephemeral vs full BYOK with lead times), subprocessors snapshot date, telemetry exclusions, retention limits, and estimated pricing delta.

deploy-bot: provision_status: transient-pool eu-west-1 created (pool-id: p-nl-2026-07). state: pending; awaiting infra sizing confirmation.

infra_tom: i'll confirm sizing & hourly delta by EOD and allocate temporary billing tag.

sec_omar: i'll prepare the subprocessors EU snapshot and an attestation PDF labeled: "subprocessors snapshot as of 2026-03-20" and share with legal for signing.

legal_sam: will prepare the scoping addendum template for POC exceptions. include retention clause, data types allowed, and acceptance of ephemeral-key exception if needed.

mike_sales: thanks team. i'll ask NordicLedger whether they'd accept the attestation + ephemeral-key flow to meet their start date. if they insist on full BYOK + contractual zero-egress, we'll propose a 2-week delay and a Private deployment plan. back in touch after customer reply. :thumbsup:
